claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in fusion plasma-facing structural alloys are controlled by coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates hinder uncontrolled dislocation pile-up or accumulation.
The precipitate-induced hindrance of dislocation accumulation improves strength.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent interfaces promote uniform or smoother dislocation motion.
Coherent nanoprecipitates relieve local stress concentrations that can cause premature crack initiation.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitates can be introduced into a tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy through targeted alloy design and processing.
Specific annealing protocols can produce a uniform distribution of coherent nanoprecipitates in the proposed alloy.
Approximately 800 °C is a relevant elevated-temperature testing condition for tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys proposed for plasma-facing applications.
Testing in an inert or vacuum atmosphere prevents oxidation from confounding the mechanical response.
At high temperature, the SCCP-treated alloy will have greater plastic strain or ductility than the homogeneous solid-solution baseline.
At high temperature, the SCCP-treated alloy will have greater toughness than the homogeneous solid-solution baseline.
The SCCP-treated alloy will show less strain localization than the homogeneous baseline.
The SCCP-treated alloy will show less premature crack initiation than the homogeneous baseline.
A tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy containing SCCPs can retain high strength at 800 °C.
The proposed mechanism should extend broadly to high-temperature refractory or high-entropy alloys intended for plasma-facing fusion components.
The exact quantitative improvement in plasticity and toughness, including interactions with grain size and secondary phases, remains experimentally undetermined.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in high-temperature ductility and toughness, together with failure to establish precipitate-mediated dislocation behavior, would falsify the hypothesis.
